newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Japan expected to pick up towards yearend.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Japan expected to pick up towards yearend.

text.p: Japanese equities analysts expect a sluggish performance from the Nikkei 225 until the end of the first half, but forecast a boost towards the end of 1997, a Reuters survey of equity forecasts showed on Wednesday.
Ten analysts based in Tokyo gave an average end-year prediction of just over 20,800 for the index, compared with the close on March 12 of 18,183.

The anticipated 14.4 percent rise from current levels is slightly more cautious than forecasts made at the end of 1996. Then, analysts said they expected the Nikkei to hit nearly 23,500 by the end of this year.
Analysts said the rate of growth was being dictated by government plans to promote deregulation and administrative reforms in the first half.

The analysts predicted a year of consolidation in 1997, with a gradual increase from the anticipated levels at the end of this year. The average forecast for end-1998 was for a rise of nearly 15 percent from current levels to more than 21,000.
TADAHIRO KAMOGAWA, GENERAL MANAGER YAMAICHI SECURITIES:
"The likely economic slowdown in the April to June period should be a one-off event. The economy should rebound afterwards, led by higher private spending.

"Various (economic) policy changes should be made public by June and that should give the market some direction. Worries over Japan's financial system should peak out by the latter half of 1997, which will be encouraging for domestic and foreign investors."
